detections.evidence_quote: Some people said closing schools for so long was pointless and would cause much worse collateral damage to kids, and they were right.
detections.summary: Hosts argue that early COVID uncertainty is no longer an excuse and endorse the claim that prolonged school closures caused disproportionate harm to kids.

detections.evidence_quote: there's at least a 50-50 chance that the virus could have begun in the lab in Wuhan that was doing gain-of-function research on that virus.
detections.summary: Hosts revisit the Wuhan lab-leak/gain-of-function origin theory, arguing it was wrongly dismissed as a conspiracy theory and is now widely credited.

detections.evidence_quote: Of course, it wasn't a conspiracy theory, and it wasn't owned by Steve Bannon.
detections.summary: Speaker corrects a past media label of the lab-leak theory as a conspiracy theory.

detections.evidence_quote: when COVID hit, we did a lot of stupid things because America never reacts; it only overreacts.
detections.summary: Passing joking characterization of pandemic-era behavior as national overreaction.

detections.evidence_quote: all these guys were all pushing the same thing with the with the vaccine and with all the COVID stuff.
detections.summary: Hosts argue that commentators who uniformly pushed vaccine and COVID messaging should be held accountable now that harms including injuries and rising cancer are being discussed.

detections.evidence_quote: Were you guys getting paid to say it?
detections.summary: Speaker insinuates that vaccine-promoting commentators were paid to deliver that messaging.
